questions.text: The supreme power of a state to make and enforce laws without external control is
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the ultimate law-making power, internally over citizens and externally free of foreign control.

questions.text: A constitution that requires a special procedure for its amendment is described as
questions.explanation: A rigid constitution can only be amended by a cumbersome process such as a two-thirds legislative majority and state approvals.

questions.text: The doctrine of separation of powers was propounded by
questions.explanation: Montesquieu argued in The Spirit of the Laws that legislative, executive and judicial powers should rest in separate hands.

questions.text: The main function of the judiciary is to
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets the constitution and statutes, adjudicates disputes and protects fundamental rights.

questions.text: In a federal system of government, powers are
options: shared between central and component units by the constitution
questions.explanation: Federalism constitutionally divides powers so that neither level of government is subordinate to the other.

questions.text: A one-party system is usually associated with
questions.explanation: Where only one party is legal, opposition is suppressed and power is concentrated, which is characteristic of authoritarian states.

questions.text: The electoral system in which a candidate with the highest number of votes wins, regardless of a majority, is
questions.explanation: First past the post awards the seat to the leading candidate even without more than half of the votes cast.

questions.text: The civil service is characterised by all of the following except
questions.explanation: Civil servants serve whichever government is in office and must therefore remain non-partisan.

questions.text: The 1914 amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria was carried out by
questions.explanation: Sir Frederick Lugard amalgamated the two protectorates in 1914 largely for administrative and fiscal convenience.

questions.text: The constitution that introduced federalism into Nigeria was the
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 formally made Nigeria a federation with autonomous regions.

questions.text: Indirect rule in Northern Nigeria succeeded largely because of the
options: existence of a centralised emirate system
questions.explanation: The emirates already had a hierarchy of authority, taxation and courts that the British could govern through.

questions.text: The main difference between a political party and a pressure group is that a political party
questions.explanation: A pressure group seeks to influence policy from outside; a party contests elections to form government.

questions.text: The principal organ of the United Nations charged with maintaining international peace and security is the
questions.explanation: The Security Council may authorise sanctions and peacekeeping, and its five permanent members hold the veto.

questions.text: ECOWAS was established in 1975 primarily to promote
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Lagos created ECOWAS to promote trade, free movement and economic cooperation in the sub-region.

questions.text: The acquisition of citizenship by a foreigner through a legal process is known as
questions.explanation: Naturalisation grants citizenship to a qualified foreigner after a period of lawful residence and good conduct.

questions.text: Which of the following is a pillar of the rule of law as expounded by A. V. Dicey?
options: Equality of all persons before the law
Immunity of public officers from prosecution
questions.explanation: Dicey's principles are the supremacy of ordinary law, equality before the law and rights grounded in judicial decisions.

questions.text: A unitary system of government is best suited to a state that is
questions.explanation: Concentrating power at the centre works best where there are few deep regional or ethnic cleavages to accommodate.

questions.text: In a presidential system, the president is
options: both head of state and head of government
questions.explanation: The offices are fused in the presidency, unlike the parliamentary system where they are separated.

questions.text: A bicameral legislature is one that
options: has two presiding officers in one chamber
questions.explanation: Nigeria's National Assembly is bicameral, consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.text: Nigeria returned to civilian rule at the beginning of the Fourth Republic in
questions.explanation: The handover on 29 May 1999 ended fifteen years of unbroken military rule.

questions.text: The main justification for creating local government is to
options: increase the number of political appointments
bring governance closer to the grassroots
reduce the powers of state governors
questions.explanation: Local government exists to deliver services and encourage participation at community level.

questions.text: The body responsible for the conduct of federal elections in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: INEC registers voters and parties and conducts elections into federal and state offices.

questions.text: The ideology that advocates public ownership of the means of production is
questions.explanation: Socialism places the means of production under collective or state ownership to reduce inequality.

questions.text: Public corporations are established mainly to
options: provide essential services to the public
questions.explanation: They supply essential services such as power and water where private provision would be inadequate or exploitative.

questions.text: Pre-colonial Igbo society is best described as
questions.explanation: Authority was dispersed among village assemblies, age grades and title holders rather than a single monarch.

questions.text: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in
questions.explanation: The AU was formally launched in Durban in July 2002 with a broader mandate than the OAU.

questions.explanation: Only a judiciary free from executive control can guarantee impartial adjudication.

options: the units differ in resources and responsibilities
federal government has no revenue of its own
questions.explanation: Vertical and horizontal imbalances between tiers of government make a sharing formula unavoidable.
